title: Earthquakes & volcanoes
examples: What causes the Earth's plates to move?
How do we measure the strength of an earthquake?
Are volcanoes always dangerous to live near?

explain.say: Today we are learning about earthquakes and volcanoes. These are powerful forces on Earth.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: two plates meeting. Look at the ocean plate, the continental plate and the trench. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Earthquakes happen because the Earth's plates move. These large plates are constantly shifting slowly.
The friction between these plates builds up a lot of energy. When this energy is suddenly released, it causes the ground to shake. This shaking is an earthquake.

items: Energy is released as seismic waves

explain.say: We measure the size of an earthquake using its magnitude. The Richter scale measures the energy released by the shaking.
Volcanoes are openings in the Earth's crust. They erupt when hot, melted rock called magma pushes through to the surface.
In everyday life, plate boundaries are always at work. The San Andreas Fault in California shows plate movement clearly. This area has experienced many significant earthquakes over time.

faq.q: Why do earthquakes happen at plate boundaries?
faq.a: Plate boundaries are where the Earth's giant plates meet. The interaction at these edges causes friction and stress to build up. This stress eventually releases energy as an earthquake.
asks: Where is the best place to feel an earthquake?
What causes the shaking at plate edges?

faq.a: Volcanoes form when magma, which is melted rock, rises from deep within the Earth. This magma finds a weak spot in the crust and forces its way out.
asks: What is the difference between magma and lava?
Why do some places have many volcanoes?

faq.q: Is the Richter scale accurate for all earthquakes?
faq.a: The Richter scale is a common way to measure earthquake magnitude. However, scientists use other tools too, as different scales measure different things.
asks: What does the number on the Richter scale mean?
Can we predict when an earthquake will happen?

faq.q: What is the difference between magma and lava?
faq.a: Magma is melted rock found underground beneath the surface. Lava is the name for that same melted rock once it has erupted onto the Earth's surface.
Volcanoes can be very dangerous, but they are also part of Earth's natural cycle. Scientists study them to predict and prepare for eruptions.
asks: What should I do near a volcano?

facts: Earthquakes are caused by the sudden release of energy in the Earth's crust.
The Richter scale measures the magnitude, or size, of an earthquake.
Magma is molten rock found beneath the Earth's surface.
Lava is magma that has reached the Earth's surface.

quiz.say: If two plates are sliding past each other, what force builds up?
quiz.why: When plates grind past each other, the rubbing creates immense stress that builds up over time.

wrong.0: Magma pressure relates to volcanoes, not the sliding of plates.
wrong.1: Water erosion wears away rock over time, but it does not build up tectonic stress.
wrong.3: Tidal forces are caused by gravity from the Moon and Sun, not plate rubbing.

quiz.say: What is the best way to measure the energy released by an earthquake?
quiz.why: The Richter scale is the standard measurement tool for quantifying earthquake energy release.

wrong.0: Depth tells us how deep underground the quake started, not its power.
wrong.1: This rate measures how fast plates move apart, not the energy released in a single event.
wrong.3: Wave speed tells us how fast the shaking travels, not how strong the quake was.

quiz.say: When magma reaches the surface, what is it called?
quiz.why: The key difference is location: magma is underground, and lava is on the surface.

wrong.0: Eruption is the event of coming out, not the substance itself.
wrong.1: Ash is the solid material that gets thrown out, not the liquid rock.
wrong.3: Magma is the term used for melted rock while it is still deep inside the Earth.
